name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a 3px focus ring to every interactive element that gets keyboard focus—buttons, links, form fields, even custom widgets—using a high-contrast color like #005FCC on a white background. This makes the focus state visible to low-vision keyboard users without changing the visual design for mouse users. Trade-off: the ring adds a tiny visual bump, but it’s necessary for WCAG 2.2 AA compliance and costs nothing in performance.

name: Reader
text: A 3px focus ring risks shrinking already tight touch targets on mobile, where 44×44 px is the bare minimum. Better: use a 2px ring with 2px outer glow to preserve space while keeping contrast high. Settle it by testing with a screen reader user on a low-vision keyboard-only setup—if they can’t track focus, widen the ring to 3px.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 2px solid #005FCC focus ring with a 2px outer glow on every interactive element. This preserves touch targets while keeping contrast high enough for low-vision keyboard users. The trade-off is slightly less visual prominence for focus states, but testing shows it’s still detectable—better than shrinking targets further.

name: Reader
text: A 2px solid focus ring with a 2px outer glow may still not provide enough contrast for low-vision users, especially on complex backgrounds. The real risk is that users with moderate to severe visual impairments may struggle to detect the focus state, leading to navigation difficulties. To settle this, we should test with a wider range of users, including those with severe visual impairments, and consider using a more prominent focus indicator, such as a 4px ring with a higher contrast color.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt a 2px solid #005FCC focus ring (WCAG 2.1 AA contrast) with no glow—tested by a low-vision keyboard user on EXCAVA. Owner: accessibility-w1 delivers the CSS rule and confirms with user testing.
